name: browser
description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation
one_liner: A browser built from scratch to be driven by robots and AI, not humans — no tabs, no rendering flourishes, just fetching and reading web pages using far less memory and time than a normal browser.
buyer: A startup running web-scraping or AI-agent infrastructure at scale who is currently paying a large cloud bill to run hundreds of full Chrome instances.
business_use_cases: A web-scraping-as-a-service company swaps Chrome for this in its crawling fleet and cuts server costs by running far more concurrent sessions per machine.
An AI agent startup uses it as the 'eyes' for autonomous browsing agents that need to read and act on web pages without the overhead of a full browser.
A QA/monitoring company runs uptime and content checks on thousands of client websites on a fraction of the hardware a Selenium/Chrome grid would need.

money_ideas.idea: A hosted 'browser-as-a-service' API that bills per page fetched, undercutting existing headless-Chrome cloud providers on price because of the lower resource footprint.
Paid managed fleets with SLAs for companies that need reliable large-scale scraping but don't want to run the infrastructure.

steal_this: Spin up a cheap 'fetch any URL as clean markdown/JSON' API on top of this this weekend and sell it to indie AI-agent builders who are currently overpaying a scraping API for the same thing.
